commit.subject: Make AsyncWorkerThreadPool into an actual pool
commit.message:
Make AsyncWorkerThreadPool into an actual pool

Previously AsyncWorkerThreadPool would spawn a new thread per task,
which doesn't scale as we look at depending more on the task system
to handle a variety of smaller tasks off the main thread.

This change makes it into an actual thread pool of a fixed size to
reduce the per-task overhead.

Note that AsyncWorkerThreadPool is only used in applications that choose
not to override DawnPlatform::CreateWorkerTaskPool, such as the Dawn
tests. When used in Chromium the browser supplies it's own
WorkerTaskPool.

Bug: 430452846
Change-Id: I14d9d8aabd340732d0ab187b3f3e08efeab08a17

commit.subject: [ir] Reject non-constructible types for `construct`
commit.message:
[ir] Reject non-constructible types for `construct`

The fuzzer was constructing texture types, which is not valid.

There's a special case to allow non-constructible types for the MSL
backend, which does put textures and pointers inside structures that
are still considered constructible from MSL's perspective.

Update a few other bespoke MSL types to flag that they are indeed
constructible.

Fixed: 431185304
Change-Id: I03b99165a4ab9d7cfac95d97c3ea0c64da907bf8

commit.subject: [dawn][opengl] Add typed integer for GL-specific indices.
commit.message:
[dawn][opengl] Add typed integer for GL-specific indices.

The OpenGL backend has a few more kinds of indices used in the zoo of
indices for bindings: a flattened binding index across a whole pipeline
layout and the GL texture units. Add typed integer for them so it's
clearer what an index is instead of just GLuint.

The OpenGL backend has a few more kinds of indices used in the zoo of
indices for bindings: a flattened binding index across a whole pipeline
layout and the GL texture units. Add typed integer for them so it's
clearer what an index is instead of just GLuint.

Change-Id: Id9f26598cf05059d4157b7ce81f5d0a6c5717a74

commit.subject: [exit-time-destructors] kBenchmarkInputs as no-destructor
commit.message:
[exit-time-destructors] kBenchmarkInputs as no-destructor

This CL makes `kBenchmarkInputs` a `[[clang::no_destroy]]` object,
preventing its destructor from running. In general the style guide
prohibits exit-time destructors[1]. For this particular case, the use
seems harmless, however with work to make `-Wexit-time-destructors` a
default warning in Chromium, this particular generated target gets on
the way.

[1] https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html#Static_and_Global_Variables

Change-Id: Idb3b15bcfab5e53684f361ce7ac81f7f42440d67

commit.subject: [dawn][opengl] Support combined samplers for binding_array
commit.message:
[dawn][opengl] Support combined samplers for binding_array

The OpenGL backend needs to transform all of the uses of textures into
combined samplers and textures. binding_array needs to be supported
there by using multiple texture units per combined sampler if needed.

Changes are:
 - In PipelineGL loop over the binding_array if needed when assigning
   texture units.
 - SizedBindingArrayTests are enabled on OpenGL.
 - Creation of the placeholder sampler in PipelineGL is changed to use
   the reentrant Device::CreateSampler which has a known default
   descriptor.
 - One of the binding array tests for oversized array in the BGL had the
   WGSL binding_array with the same size as the BGL which was not what
   was intended to be tested.
 - Adds a suppression for a test that's not passing on GL yet.
 - Adds a targeted test for the logic added in PipelineGL.

Bug: 411573957
Change-Id: I8144c68466e8073144db9b222df2a9845b1d4f51

commit.subject: Kotlin: Make WebGPU container class API more Kotlin idiomatic
commit.message:
Kotlin: Make WebGPU container class API more Kotlin idiomatic

Replace nullable surface with a getter that will raise an exception if called in a context where the surface is not present.

The only circumstances in which a surface is not present is if the caller did not pass in an Android surface when the WebGPU creator was called.

Test: ./gradlew connectedAndroidTest

commit.subject: Range Analysis: Compute range of built-in call `max`
commit.message:
Range Analysis: Compute range of built-in call `max`

This patch computes the range of a core built-in call `max`.
- When both `a` and `b` are constant values, the range of
  `max(a, b)` will also be a constant value.
- When the range of `a` is [min1, max1] and the range of `b` is
  [min2, max2], the range of `max(a, b)` is `[max(min1, min2),
  max(max1, max2)]`.
- The ranges that represent the whole range of `i32` or `u32`
  are treated as invalid ones (e.g. max(a, i32::kLowestValue)).

Bug: 348701956
Test: tint_unittests
Change-Id: Id2c650b289da7221744c28ca92ca92d8c0a84b6b

commit.subject: [tint] Run `Robustness` transform prior to `PreventInfiniteLoops`
commit.message:
[tint] Run `Robustness` transform prior to `PreventInfiniteLoops`

This patch moves the execution of the `Robustness` transform prior
to the `PreventInfiniteLoops` transform. Below are the reasons:

`PreventInfiniteLoops` has stricter restrictions on the loop than
the ones in the Integer Range Analysis in `Robustness` transform
(e.g. `PreventInfiniteLoops` doesn't support `LessThanEqual` and
`GreaterThanEqual`, and has additional requirements on the loop
body). After `PreventInfiniteLoops` is executed, another loop control
variable will be inserted in the loop initialization block, which
is not acceptable for Integer Range Analysis.

Note that in GLSL backend `Robustness` has already been put prior
to `PreventInfiniteLoops`.

Bug: 348701956
Change-Id: I82bf0758c5892f4136662a20eb597dafab4117e0

commit.subject: [tint] Run `Robustness` transform before `PreventInfiniteLoops`
commit.message:
[tint] Run `Robustness` transform before `PreventInfiniteLoops`

This patch moves the execution of the `Robustness` transform prior to
the `PreventInfiniteLoops` transform and the `BinaryPolyfill`
transform.

Below are the reasons:
- `PreventInfiniteLoops` has stricter restrictions on the loop than
  the ones in the Integer Range Analysis in `Robustness` transform
  (e.g. `PreventInfiniteLoops` doesn't accept `LessThanEqual` and
  `GreaterThanEqual`, and has additional requirements on the loop
  body). After `PreventInfiniteLoops` is executed, another loop
  control variable will be inserted in the loop initialization block,
  which will make the loop fail the test in Integer Range Analysis.
- `BinaryPolyfill` transform may replace the `divide` operator with
  a polyfill, which cannot be accepted by the current Integer Range
  Analysis algorithm.

Note that in GLSL backend `Robustness` has already been put before
`PreventInfiniteLoops`.

Bug: 348701956
Change-Id: I82bf0758c5892f4136662a20eb597dafab4117e0

commit.message:
[m139] [graphite] [metal] Emit MSL in error message on failed pipeline creation

We currently emit MSL when shader module compilation fails, but not when
the subsequent render pipeline creation fails. Keep the MSL around a bit
longer so that we can emit it on render pipeline creation failure.

commit.message:
[graphite] [metal] Emit MSL in error message on failed pipeline creation

We currently emit MSL when shader module compilation fails, but not when
the subsequent render pipeline creation fails. Keep the MSL around a bit
longer so that we can emit it on render pipeline creation failure.

commit.subject: Add E2E tests for 16-bit UNORM/SNORM format capabilities
commit.message:
Add E2E tests for 16-bit UNORM/SNORM format capabilities

This commit introduces end-to-end tests for R16Unorm, R16Snorm, RG16Unorm, RG16Snorm, RGBA16Unorm, and RGBA16Snorm texture formats. These tests validate their support for RENDER_ATTACHMENT, blendable, multisampling and STORAGE_BINDING (read-only and write-only) with the `TextureFormatsTier1` feature being enabled.

Reland "Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"""

Original change's description:
> Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading""
>
> This is a reland of commit e579b628e5d5276086b6a2eaefa1718586bc7e18
>
> Add dawn_force_system_component_load for projects (like Skia) which
> require that Dawn load all compiler DLL from System32. Best security
> is to leave the default value which (now) loads compiler DLLs from the
> same directory as Dawn code.
>
> On Chromium builds (such as x86) which do not build DXC, place the
> DLLs from the SDK into the build folder to appease infra tools that
> copy the DLLs unconditionally.
>
> Improve DAWN_USE_BUILT_DXC to use the #define to skip loading the DLLs
> altogether.
>
> Original change's description:
> > Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"
> >
> > This is a reland of commit e4d4669d79501b1acdd2bf017ba491b611d741da
> >
> > Remove build_with_chromium statements in test GN files that copy
> > DLLs. Rely on copies instructions which already exist with the D3D12
> > files.
> >
> > To appease Skia builds which do not depend on the Windows SDK,
> > fallback to system FXC if the local directory version is not found.
> >
> > Original change's description:
> > > Improve DX compiler library loading
> > >
> > > Previously, DX compiler DLLs were loaded using LoadLibrary with no path.
> > > D3D12 compiler DLLs were further sourced from the local user's SDK
> > > directory as a fallback.
> > >
> > > For better security, load DX compiler DLLs using full paths, with
> > > SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS for better security. Scenarios
> > > such as Skia and x86 builds where we need dawn_use_built_dxc will
> > > fallback to FXC. No fallbacks to local user SDK directories.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Fixes TSAN issues when running without implicit sync.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Fixes TSAN issues when running without implicit sync.

- When running without implicit synchronization, there isn't a lock
  protecting access to the Defer object in Device. This resulted in
  TSAN complaining about potential data races. Instead, if we are
  not running with implicit synchronization, we don't need to create
  a valid lock, nor create defer object, so just use a static global
  placeholder value.

Change-Id: I9920de121c4443f3f6453f02228fc6c0a2d0e932

commit.subject: Fix ApiObjectList::Destroy() race
commit.message:
Fix ApiObjectList::Destroy() race

There is a race if ApiObjectList::Destroy() is going to destroy an
object and another thread drops the last reference to the object at the
same time. The other thread won't run DestroyImpl() but it will call
`delete this` and delete the object resulting in a use-after-free.
Keeping the ApiObjectList lock during DestroyImpl() calls won't work due
to https://crbug.com/42240929.

Have ApiObjectList::Destroy() acquire a reference to all of the
objects. RefCounted::TryAddRef() is added to expose the try to add
reference functionality that WeakRefData was already using.

Bug: 396294899, 429112750

commit.subject: Fix ApiObjectList::Destroy() race
commit.message:
Fix ApiObjectList::Destroy() race

There is a race if ApiObjectList::Destroy() is going to destroy an
object and another thread drops the last reference to the object at the
same time. The other thread won't run DestroyImpl() but it will call
`delete this` and delete the object resulting in a use-after-free.
Keeping the ApiObjectList lock during DestroyImpl() calls won't work due
to https://crbug.com/42240929.

Have ApiObjectList::Destroy() acquire a reference to all of the
objects. RefCounted::TryAddRef() is added to expose the try to add
reference functionality that WeakRefData was already using.

commit.subject: Use vector to hold objects to destroy
commit.message:
Use vector to hold objects to destroy

ApiObjectList::Destroy() moved the objects it is going to destoy to a
temporary LinkedList. ApiObjectList::Untrack() returns true if the
object is in any list. If another thread runs
ApiObjectBase::DeleteThis() at the same time, that sees the objects are
in a list and proceeds to remove it from list and then destroy it. This
can result in object being removed from list and having DestroyImpl()
called on it twice.

This is fixed by using a std::vector to track the objects to destroy
instead. This avoids the double remove/destruction as
ApiObjectList::Destroy() removes all objects from the original list
under the lock.

Note there is still a problem where the if the last reference is dropped
on another thread before ApiObjectList calls DestroyImpl(). The other
thread will delete the object resulting in DestroyImpl() being a
use-after-free. That is going to fixed as a follow up.

Add unit tests to confirm that enabling the "texture-formats-tier1" feature at device creation
implicitly enables "rg11b10ufloat-renderable". Tests include RENDER_ATTACHMENT, blendable,

> [ir-to-program] Fix issue converting int32_t min.

commit.message:
[ir-to-program] Fix issue converting int32_t min.

When converting an `i32` minimum value from IR back to WGSL, we can't
just emit the number as it won't parse in WGSL. We need to emit it as an
abstract and convert that to an i32 value.

Change-Id: I173d1a78f78c8af8ab9791c8b72f879b67520276

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Fix loop continuing Phi issue.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Fix loop continuing Phi issue.

If we're propagating a value through a loop continue block, but the
continue is unreachable, then we would have skipped emitting the body
and the propagated value won't exist.

In this case, just propagate an undef value as we don't actually care
what the real value was.

Fixed: 429625248
Change-Id: If2a7269546c8c203a16c36c96b15bc21383b3aa0

commit.subject: Range Analysis: Compute range of built-in call `min`
commit.message:
Range Analysis: Compute range of built-in call `min`

This patch computes the range of a core built-in call `min`.
- When both `a` and `b` are constant values, the range of
  `min(a, b)` will also be a constant value.
- When the range of `a` is [min1, max1] and the range of `b` is
  [min2, max2], the range of min(a, b) is `[min(min1, min2),
  min(max1, max2)]`. The ranges that represent the whole range
  `i32` or `u32` are treated as invalid ones.

Bug: 348701956
Test: tint_unittests
Change-Id: Ifc67d12b23a7f3ba77250c8857bc5e9147db23b9

commit.subject: vulkan: Remove host cached requirement for mappable buffers
commit.message:
vulkan: Remove host cached requirement for mappable buffers

Using mappable buffers required a memory type that supports both host
cached and host coherent memory. No memory of this type is available on
Mali GPUs so mappable buffers weren't used.

Drop the host cached requirement since it's not strictly necessary. This
has similar performance to dropping the host coherent requirement,
except that requires adding explicit flush/invalidate memory range calls
which is a bit more complicated. Likely dawn should pick host cached
or host coherent based on some heuristic in the future.

Bug: 422798184
Change-Id: I3f2182ee362a732c130c7946b6f31709bc02a55d

commit.subject: Fail to create a device if adapter has been consumed
commit.message:
Fail to create a device if adapter has been consumed

This CL makes sure an adapter can not create a device once it has been
consumed. This behavior can be disabled by passing the
wgpu::InstanceFeatureName::MultipleDevicesPerAdapter required feature
when creating the instance.

Bug: 415825174, 419339310

[ir] Only clone let name if it's valid.

we only attempt to clone valid names. If the name is invalid, just leave
as invalid in the cloned instruction.

commit.subject: Revert "Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"""
commit.message:
Revert "Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"""

This reverts commit a45d5b2b40d12d0f650e3f8cdd70a20c853ff5a0.

Reason for revert: Causing dawn_end2end_*validation_layers_tests to
time out on UHD 770 bots
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/luci.chromium.ci/Dawn%20Win10%20x64%20Release%20%28Intel%20UHD%20770%29

Bug: 356665092
Original change's description:
> Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading""
>
> This is a reland of commit e579b628e5d5276086b6a2eaefa1718586bc7e18
>
> Add dawn_force_system_component_load for projects (like Skia) which
> require that Dawn load all compiler DLL from System32. Best security
> is to leave the default value which (now) loads compiler DLLs from the
> same directory as Dawn code.
>
> On Chromium builds (such as x86) which do not build DXC, place the
> DLLs from the SDK into the build folder to appease infra tools that
> copy the DLLs unconditionally.
>
> Improve DAWN_USE_BUILT_DXC to use the #define to skip loading the DLLs
> altogether.
>
> Original change's description:
> > Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"
> >
> > This is a reland of commit e4d4669d79501b1acdd2bf017ba491b611d741da
> >
> > Remove build_with_chromium statements in test GN files that copy
> > DLLs. Rely on copies instructions which already exist with the D3D12
> > files.
> >
> > To appease Skia builds which do not depend on the Windows SDK,
> > fallback to system FXC if the local directory version is not found.
> >
> > Original change's description:
> > > Improve DX compiler library loading
> > >
> > > Previously, DX compiler DLLs were loaded using LoadLibrary with no path.

commit.subject: Revert "Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"""
commit.message:
Revert "Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"""

This reverts commit a45d5b2b40d12d0f650e3f8cdd70a20c853ff5a0.

Reason for revert: Causing dawn_end2end_*validation_layers_tests to
time out on UHD 770 bots
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/luci.chromium.ci/Dawn%20Win10%20x64%20Release%20%28Intel%20UHD%20770%29

Bug: 356665092
Original change's description:
> Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading""
>
> This is a reland of commit e579b628e5d5276086b6a2eaefa1718586bc7e18
>
> Add dawn_force_system_component_load for projects (like Skia) which
> require that Dawn load all compiler DLL from System32. Best security
> is to leave the default value which (now) loads compiler DLLs from the
> same directory as Dawn code.
>
> On Chromium builds (such as x86) which do not build DXC, place the
> DLLs from the SDK into the build folder to appease infra tools that
> copy the DLLs unconditionally.
>
> Improve DAWN_USE_BUILT_DXC to use the #define to skip loading the DLLs
> altogether.
>
> Original change's description:
> > Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"
> >
> > This is a reland of commit e4d4669d79501b1acdd2bf017ba491b611d741da
> >
> > Remove build_with_chromium statements in test GN files that copy
> > DLLs. Rely on copies instructions which already exist with the D3D12
> > files.
> >
> > To appease Skia builds which do not depend on the Windows SDK,
> > fallback to system FXC if the local directory version is not found.
> >
> > Original change's description:
> > > Improve DX compiler library loading
> > >
> > > Previously, DX compiler DLLs were loaded using LoadLibrary with no path.
> > > D3D12 compiler DLLs were further sourced from the local user's SDK
> > > directory as a fallback.
> > >
> > > For better security, load DX compiler DLLs using full paths, with
> > > SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS for better security. Scenarios
> > > such as Skia and x86 builds where we need dawn_use_built_dxc will
> > > fallback to FXC. No fallbacks to local user SDK directories.
> > >

commit.message:
Kotlin: ensure methods don't return nullable types.

This keeps the Kotlin API simple, avoiding clients having to check the types. If they are null because of an error, an exception would have fired anyway.

Bug: 429153911
Test: Manual
Change-Id: Ifc00447fa8a0459ae69d9fe609b790e259e03677

commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Add support for `OpGroupNonUniformBroadcast`

Add support to convert the `OpGroupNonUniformBroadcast` into a
`subgroupBroadcast`. The non-constant case is not supported as we ingest
as SPIR-V 1.3 and non-constant values requires SPIR-V 1.5 or later.

Fixed: 430935990
Change-Id: I3daf0d070de9dca7d6b8e0b7c9c2835c912e2968

commit.subject: Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading""
commit.message:
Reland "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading""

This is a reland of commit e579b628e5d5276086b6a2eaefa1718586bc7e18

Original change's description:
> Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"
>
> This is a reland of commit e4d4669d79501b1acdd2bf017ba491b611d741da
>
> Remove build_with_chromium statements in test GN files that copy
> DLLs. Rely on copies instructions which already exist with the D3D12
> files.
>
> To appease Skia builds which do not depend on the Windows SDK,
> fallback to system FXC if the local directory version is not found.
>
> Original change's description:
> > Improve DX compiler library loading
> >
> > Previously, DX compiler DLLs were loaded using LoadLibrary with no path.
> > D3D12 compiler DLLs were further sourced from the local user's SDK
> > directory as a fallback.
> >
> > For better security, load DX compiler DLLs using full paths, with
> > SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS for better security. Scenarios
> > such as Skia and x86 builds where we need dawn_use_built_dxc will
> > fallback to FXC. No fallbacks to local user SDK directories.
> >
> > Bug:356665092
> > Change-Id: Ib4148f9b89da694e3868b4f3c3c329a4b06ce922
> > Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/229754
> > Reviewed-by: Corentin Wallez <cwallez@chromium.org>
> > Commit-Queue: Rafael Cintron <rafael.cintron@microsoft.com>
> > Reviewed-by: Antonio Maiorano <amaiorano@google.com>
>
> Bug: 356665092
> Change-Id: Ic05d20c47c5db3021f9e38b724bf527bfba52a5e

commit.subject: [dawn][opengl] Remove the GL-specific handling of un/filtering samplers.
commit.message:
[dawn][opengl] Remove the GL-specific handling of un/filtering samplers.

This is a likely a remnant of when the OpenGL backend was initially
created, when the WebGPU spec didn't have the concept of "non filtering
samplers". GL requires that u/int textures be used only with nearest
filtering so each sampler was split into a two, a filtering and the
respective non-filtering one. This limitation is now part of the WebGPU
validation so it is no longer necessary to handle it in the GL backend.

Also makes opengl::Sampler follow the usual pattern for ::Create (with
an Initialize method), and remove the unused and confusing
opengl::PipelineLayout::GetTextureUnitsUsed.

Bug: 411573957

commit.subject: [emdawnwebgpu] Fix string-to-int tables with Closure, enable Closure in tests
commit.message:
[emdawnwebgpu] Fix string-to-int tables with Closure, enable Closure in tests

Fix string-to-int tables by (1) making them library-level items that are
explicit dependencies (separate from $WebGPU) and (2) wrapping them to
prevent Emscripten from removing the quotation marks on the keys, that
signal to Closure that they shouldn't be minified.

This has the added benefit of Emscripten being able to eliminate tables
that are unused by the application.

Enable --closure=1 in Release builds, and add a test which explicitly
tests this. (The GetCompilationInfo tests also catch this.)

Fixed: 424836759
Bug: 377760848
Change-Id: Iaee6d18516a5d54a49869ba76ec975c12cc0cc60

commit.subject: [emdawnwebgpu] Fix wgpuQuerySetGetType
commit.message:
[emdawnwebgpu] Fix wgpuQuerySetGetType

Fix wgpuQuerySetGetType by translating the string to int.

WebGPU.QueryType.indexOf (which is slightly slower but avoids needing a
string-to-int array) wasn't possible because WebGPU.QueryType is an
object instead of an array (because the enum is sparse), so this changes
it to be a real array.

It also reduces the code size of this and other enums that are dense but
start at 1, *and* may be slightly faster for int-to-string lookups.
(BTW, Emscripten's load-and-reserialize for compiling library members
already removes the unnecessary `undefined` at the beginning of arrays
generated with an explicit `undefined` at the beginning.)

An alternative would be to store the query type in memory and implement
this in webgpu.cpp. This should reduce the overall code size but it
would not work for imported query sets. This is something we probably
should consider in the future (tracked in bug 377760848).

Add SpotTests.cpp for Emdawnwebgpu smoke/regression tests, and a test
for this (copied from the bug report).

Fixed: 429140225
Bug: 377760848
Change-Id: I41e639cf798b558cd0c330258e690b074c4b32a3

An alternative would be to store the query type in memory and implement

should consider in the future (tracked in bug 377760848).

commit.subject: [emdawnwebgpu] Fix wgpuQuerySetGetType
commit.message:
[emdawnwebgpu] Fix wgpuQuerySetGetType

Fix wgpuQuerySetGetType by translating the string to int instead of
letting JS coerce it.

WebGPU.QueryType.indexOf (which is slightly slower but avoids needing a
string-to-int array) wasn't possible because WebGPU.QueryType is an
object instead of an array (because the enum is sparse), so this changes
it to be a real array.

It also reduces the code size of this and other enums that are dense but
start at 1, *and* may be slightly faster for int-to-string lookups.
(Emscripten's load-and-reserialize for compiling library members was
already removing the unnecessary `undefined` in arrays that contained
`undefined`, but this change makes the generator avoid that too.)

An alternative would be to store the query type in memory and implement
this in webgpu.cpp. This should reduce the overall code size but it
would not work for imported query sets. This is something we probably
should consider in the future (tracked in bug 377760848).

Add SpotTests.cpp for Emdawnwebgpu smoke/regression tests, and a test
for this (copied from the bug report).

Fixed: 429140225
Bug: 377760848
Change-Id: I41e639cf798b558cd0c330258e690b074c4b32a3

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Split maxImmediateSize into a separate limits group
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Split maxImmediateSize into a separate limits group

Tiering is applied per group of limits such that if any of tier (n+1)
can't be supported, all limits go down to tier (n). maxImmediateSize
shouldn't be grouped with the OTHER limits because its tiers don't line
up with the others, causing maxVertexAttributes to be lowered
unnecessarily (it's the only limit in the OTHER group that varies from
tier0 to tier1).

commit.subject: D3D11: Remove DXGISharedHandle STM without fences tests.
commit.message:
D3D11: Remove DXGISharedHandle STM without fences tests.

DXGISharedHandle without fences require certain restrictions. For
example, the ID3D11Texture2D generated from the DXGISharedHandle must be
reused. We cannot use that same DXGISharedHandle to create duplicated
textures. Because even if we use the same DXGISharedHandle to import to
the same device, it will still create a different ID3D11Texture2D
object. And these texture objects require fences to properly
synchronize.

Unfortunately, not every base STM test code understands
these restrictions, so disable the tests' variant entirely.

We already have tests using ID3D11Texture2D without fences below. They
pretty much should cover almost the same code paths albeit without
using DXGISharedHandle to create ID3D11Texture2D.

This fixes several recent failures on UHD770 bots. Note: this is not
a fix for the "did not complete" hangs on the same bots which also
started happening recently but much earlier.

Bug: chromium:429093435
Change-Id: I9e07d1e57e679e1b564840f57656f15a605c60d7

commit.subject: Fix ApiObjectList::Destroy() race
commit.message:
Fix ApiObjectList::Destroy() race

There is a race if ApiObjectList::Destroy() is going to destroy an
object and another thread drops the last reference to the object at the
same time. The other thread won't run DestroyImpl() but it will call
`delete this` and destroy the object resulting in a use-after-free.
Keeping the ApiObjectList lock during DestroyImpl() calls won't work due
to https://crbug.com/42240929.

Have ApiObjectList::Destroy() acquire a reference to all of the
objects. This requires adding RefCounted::TryAddRef() for this specific
use case. ApiObjectList is made a friend class and TryAddRef() is kept
protected so it's not generally usable.

Bug: 396294899, 4291127501
Change-Id: Ib0dcad57bccac87835c2c6d1cab3609cf0e53ee7

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Split maxImmediateSize into a separate limits group
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Split maxImmediateSize into a separate limits group

Tiering is applied per group of limits such that if any of tier (n+1)
can't be supported, all limits go down to tier (n). maxImmediateSize
shouldn't be grouped with the OTHER limits because its tiers don't line
up with the others, causing maxVertexAttributes to be lowered
unnecessarily (it's the only limit in the OTHER group that varies from
tier0 to tier1).

Fixed: 430602495
Test: manually checked webgpureport.org in local windows chromium build
Fixed: 430371785

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Split maxImmediateSize into a separate limits group
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Split maxImmediateSize into a separate limits group

Tiering is applied per group of limits such that if any of tier (n+1)
can't be supported, all limits go down to tier (n). maxImmediateSize
shouldn't be grouped with the OTHER limits because its tiers don't line
up with the others, causing maxVertexAttributes to be lowered
unnecessarily (it's the only limit in the OTHER group that varies from
tier0 to tier1).

Fixed: 430602495
Test: manually checked webgpureport.org in local windows chromium build

commit.message:
[dawn] Add and enforce WGPUInstanceFeatureName_ShaderSourceSPIRV

This adds a new instance feature ShaderSourceSPIRV which is required to
use the WGPUShaderSourceSPIRV extension struct for CreateShaderModule.

This is enforced alongside DisallowSpirv - that must be disabled AND
this must be enabled in order to use SPIRV.

commit.subject: D3D12: Initialize `mZeroBuffer` from CPU with BufferMapExtendedUsages
commit.message:
D3D12: Initialize `mZeroBuffer` from CPU with BufferMapExtendedUsages

This patch creates `mZeroBuffer` as a mappable buffer and
initializes it from CPU when `BufferMapExtendedUsages` is supported
on the current physical device. This change will save another
memory allocation in DynamicUploader and may help workaround some
issues that happen in the device initialization.

Bug: 42242085, 427605329
Change-Id: I34d6715847d3a28a03d48b6eef93d2ad2a612e09

commit.subject: [dawn] Enable TINT_BUILD_SPV_READER in Wasm
commit.message:
[dawn] Enable TINT_BUILD_SPV_READER in Wasm

Fix a bug where TINT_BUILD_SPV_READER would be disabled in builds that
had dawn_wasm, even for non-Wasm targets. (One GN build can contain both
Wasm and non-Wasm targets.)

We could probably just fix it to use is_wasm instead of dawn_wasm, but
there should be no reason to disable the SPIR-V Reader in Wasm builds.
(In fact, we definitely should support it so that Tint can be chained
with an HLSL or GLSL compiler in Wasm.)

CreateShaderModuleFromASM didn't work in Wasm because it depends on
wgpu::DawnShaderModuleSPIRVOptionsDescriptor. It's only used in one test
file, so move it to that test file unmodified.

commit.message:
Support "immediate" address space in MSL IR backend

This CL adds support for "immediate" address space in the MSL IR
backend.

buffer and a options to provide binding point info for it.

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Make AddOperandToTerminator smarter.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Make AddOperandToTerminator smarter.

The only case where we need to fill in the terminator operand later is
if an `OpPhi` refers to a value after the phi. This means, we can just
add any constant value, or any known value to the terminator
immediately.

Bug: 429625248
Change-Id: I1d25fb70c4cfe03799a7e71517fac20b226d23f8

commit.subject: D3D11: Add BeginAccess's option to skip fence signaling.
commit.message:
D3D11: Add BeginAccess's option to skip fence signaling.

Previously the ability to skip fence singaling was decided when creating
a STM via a creation's descriptor's flag. This CL adds a new option in
STM's BeginAccessDescriptor to dynamically decide whether to skip fence
signaling even after the STM is created.

This allows use cases where:
- A shared image's fence signaling would be initially disabled.
- After WebGPU's first access on this shared image, fence signaling
would be enforced.

The old option will be removed once all clients are updated to use
the new option.

Bug: chromium:429093435
Change-Id: If6bab8749d96bd667a88a3e661b1ffa066481102

commit.message:
D3D11: Allow dynamically skipping fence signals in BeginAccess

Previously, fence signaling for a Shared Texture Manager (STM) was
configured only at creation. This change adds a new option to
BeginAccessDescriptor to control fence signaling dynamically at the time
of access.

This enables use cases where a shared image can initially have fence
signaling disabled and then enforce it after the first WebGPU access.

The older creation-time option will be removed once clients adopt this
new descriptor.

commit.subject: D3D11: Use blocking waits for last submitted serial in DelayFlushQueue
commit.message:
D3D11: Use blocking waits for last submitted serial in DelayFlushQueue

Previously, D3D11's DelayFlushQueue relied on ID3D11Query for
command buffer completion signals. While ID3D11Query is generally
efficient, waiting for it often involved CPU-intensive spin-waiting,
which could hinder the use of less powerful CPU cores. This update
introduces a minor but significant optimization: by utilizing a
blocking Win32 event for the last submitted serial's wait, we
eliminate spin-waiting and improve overall CPU resource management.

Bug: chromium:430308396
Change-Id: I3965e20b103d39b2bd8e464e14692dd1bc9a8a7c

commit.subject: Cache VkFramebuffers (re-reland)
commit.message:
Cache VkFramebuffers (re-reland)

Creation of VkFramebuffers is more expensive than expected on mobile
devices, so this introduces a framebuffer cache to reduce that
overhead.

Previous attempt at landing was reverted after an MSan error on Linux.

Prior to that, had trouble landing due to crashes reported in
https://crbug.com/425093010.

Discovered that the likely reason for the crashes was that Vulkan may
reuse handle values for things like image views, making them
inappropriate for use as cache keys, as I was doing previously.
Refactored this CL to use explicit unique IDs instead, which resolved
the problems on the hardware I tested against.

Bug: 416088623
Change-Id: Ic22483f0d5388ab8ea3fc307bcc69910d6699888

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Split maxImmediateSize into a separate limits group
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Split maxImmediateSize into a separate limits group

Tiering is applied per group of limits such that if any of tier (n+1)
can't be supported, all limits go down to tier (n). maxImmediateSize
shouldn't be grouped with the OTHER limits because its tiers don't line
up with the others, causing maxVertexAttributes to be lowered
unnecessarily (it's the only limit in the OTHER group that varies from
tier0 to tier1).

Test: manually checked webgpureport.org in local windows chromium build
Fixed: 430371785
Bug: 430344935
Change-Id: Ibd1901c08aed2d471591adc4755a802ca866a1bd

Tint: Move ChangeImmediateToUniform Transform to Core IR Transform

ChangeImmediateToUniform could be used by hlsl, msl and glsl to support
immediate address space.

Move this transform from hlsl writer to core ir transform to allow other
backends to use it.

Bug: 366291600
Change-Id: Ib54716983a1d3312291c794a96b96d60ae538b78

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Build the texture worklist after replacing functions.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Build the texture worklist after replacing functions.

When processing the user call instructions to replace texture variables
we may fork/delete functions. But, if the instruction we delete is one
that we were going to replace the texture builtin call, we'll get
invalid arguments.

So, process all the variable changes, and then collect up the builtins
to process.

Bug: 428007402
Change-Id: I6b9f66552fbd06ae7535d9386d2054dcdf9da457

commit.subject: [tint] Abs polyfill for all backends
commit.message:
[tint] Abs polyfill for all backends

Now that the signed arithmetic polyfill has landed [0] the workaround
for abs (as max(x,-x)) will now function correctly.

The issue with abs(i32) was only proven to be observed on intel and
nvidia but have have chosen to proactively extend this fix to all
backends and devices. This decisions was made based on the polyfill
being very low overhead and assuming a commonality between all
backend compilers (LLVM).

commit.subject: Fix Linux compat driver tags
commit.message:
Fix Linux compat driver tags

Fixes the driver tags used by compat CTS expectations on Linux. Many
expectations currently use driver tags which are only valid on Windows,
which is causing tests to start failing with a CL applied that makes
platform-specific driver tags only get produced on the relevant
platforms.

commit.message:
Move/rename immediateSize and maxImmediateSize to core structs

Since there's no longer an extension struct for the limits, this removes
tests for it, and uses new logic for setting/validating the limit:
- It's 0 by default, instead of 16

  Undefined can be requested for the limit.

I couldn't find any other projects depending on immediates, so I just
went ahead and changed everything in one go.

commit.subject: Immediates: promote/rename, use limit only, remove feature
commit.message:
Immediates: promote/rename, use limit only, remove feature

- Promote/rename immediateSize and maxImmediateSize to match webgpu.h.
  - Also updates all related names, for consistency.
- Since maxImmediateSize is now core, it defaults to 0 instead of 16.
  - Vulkan backend now needs to explicitly set it, others keep it as 0.
- Since there's no longer an extension struct for the limits, we also
  need new rules for how it's validated. Keeping the feature with the
  limit introduces questions about how the feature and the limit
  interact (what happens if you request one but not the other?), so
  instead this removes the feature entirely and gates maxImmediateSize>0
  on AllowUnsafeAPIs.
  - This simplifies some validation, as it all relies on
    maxImmediateSize and not the feature. Only
    AdapterBase::UpdateLimits() needs to care about the toggle.
- In Wasm, pass maxImmediateSize through but only if it's > 0.

No other projects seem to depend on immediates, so this changes
everything at once without any deprecations.

Fixed: 415086848
Change-Id: I980856fee5b5ec4ff98444291c410f5ab35bc178

commit.message:
Immediates: promote/rename, use limit only, remove feature

- Promote/rename immediateSize and maxImmediateSize to match webgpu.h.
  - Avoided renaming most related symbols, to reduce the size of the CL.
- Since maxImmediateSize is now core, it defaults to 0 instead of 16.
  - Vulkan backend now needs to explicitly set it, others keep it as 0.
- Since there's no longer an extension struct for the limits, we also
  need new rules for how it's validated. Keeping the feature with the
  limit introduces questions about how the feature and the limit
  interact (what happens if you request one but not the other?), so
  instead this removes the feature entirely and gates maxImmediateSize>0
  on AllowUnsafeAPIs.
  - This simplifies some validation, as it all relies on
    maxImmediateSize and not the feature. Only
    AdapterBase::UpdateLimits() needs to care about the toggle, and
    SetImmediateData needs to explicitly error if maxImmediateSize=0.
  - The WGSL feature is gated on AllowUnsafeAPIs, along with other
    existing experimental features.
- In Wasm, pass maxImmediateSize through, but only if it's > 0.

No other projects seem to depend on immediates, so this changes
everything at once without any deprecations.

Fixed: 415086848
Change-Id: I980856fee5b5ec4ff98444291c410f5ab35bc178

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Fixes TSAN race for new the Defer in DeviceGuard.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Fixes TSAN race for new the Defer in DeviceGuard.

- Skia TSAN found that there can be a race since we were null-ing out
  the Defer object without the device lock. Instead of doing without
  the lock, make Defer movable and move the Device Defer to be owned
  by he guard while still holding the lock. This way we don't have
  the potential race where another thread tries to set the Defer
  object while another thread is in the middle of deleting it.

Bug: 430047923
Cq-Include-Trybots: dawn-try-linux-tsan-rel
Include-Ci-Only-Tests: true
Change-Id: I112af3a3a3e6eb0cc1802f415277bd6e12504a78

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Update access mode on storage buffers.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Update access mode on storage buffers.

WGSL doesn't have the concept of `NonWritable` on a structure member,
but if every structure member is marked as `NonWritable` then we can
treat the structure itself as `NonWritable`. Update the IR reader to
honour this access mode.

Bug: 429447716
Change-Id: I6d62898d8703671345330085a0164e4cced21636

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Fix incorrect switch/loop exits.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Fix incorrect switch/loop exits.

In the case of an `if` where one of the branches jumps to a switch/loop
merge, and the other branch goes to the if merge which also jumps to the
switch/loop merge, from an IR perspective those two SPIR-V blocks would
refer to the same IR block. In this case, we need to differentiate by
looking at the `BranchConditional` and determining if we need to handle
this special terminator decision.

Bug: 42250952
Change-Id: I19d289bc455d7714b62898afc88ea16bd013a6fa

commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Handle Phi in loop body.

It's possible to have a PHI in a loop body, that isn't in the loop
header itself. In this case, the incoming branches end up being the
header, and unreachable blocks. Handle by ignoring anything other then
the header block in this case.

Change-Id: Idb26c0ab81cdccb64c2d101ecd3bcb155c94e6ef

commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Add OpSpecConstantComposite id's to the id stack.

When creating a constant composite we were replacing the id meaning, but
not inserting the ID into the scope stack, so it did not appear to be
in scope when subsequently used.

Use the `AddValue` helper instead of inserting the value directly so
it's added to the id scope stack.

Bug: 429651458
Change-Id: I77db090d5f2fe59aa92ce31818cb679369ea99d9

commit.subject: Use vector to hold objects to destroy
commit.message:
Use vector to hold objects to destroy

ApiObjectList::Destroy() moved the objects it is going to destoy to a
temporary LinkedList. ApiObjectList::Untrack() returns true if the
object is in any list. If another thread runs
ApiObjectBase::DeleteThis() at the same time, that sees the objects are
in a list and proceeds to remove it from list and then destroy it. This
can result in object being removed from list and having DestroyImpl()
called on it twice.

This is fixed by using a std::vector to track the objects to destroy
instead. This avoids the double remove/destruction as
ApiObjectList::Destroy() removes all objects from the original list
under the lock.

Note there is still a problem where the if the last reference is dropped
on another thread before ApiObjectList calls DestroyImpl(). The other
thread delete the object resulting in DestroyImpl() being a
use-after-free. That is going to fixed as a follow up.

Bug: 429112750, 396294899
Change-Id: I9e8a809c653a1565d1dfbb4a7be48c91a644f540
